label.title: U.S. Military Involvement and the War on Terror

claims.claim_text: Eleven years of continuous military operations and repeated deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan have stretched U.S. forces and strained their families.
Americans have been subject to terrorist attacks.
The War on Terror is ongoing.
America has declared war against terrorists.

The war in Iraq distracted the United States from confronting many of the most fundamental national security challenges facing the United States, including the danger posed by international terrorist organizations that threaten the American homeland.
U.S. troops are being routinely killed in Iraq.
U.S. service members are in harm's way in the war against terror.
A generation of American efforts to slow proliferation of weapons of mass destruction has unraveled as Iraq defied the international community.
The war in Iraq has overextended America's armed services.
The capacity to inflict damage from nuclear, biological, and cyber attacks is spreading to other countries and potentially to terrorist groups.
America faces a new and rapidly evolving threat from terrorism and international crime.
U.S. wars in the Middle East have left a bloody legacy, killing over a million people.
